newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Flesh-eating dinosaur dug up in Patagonia.
newsitem.headline: Flesh-eating dinosaur dug up in Patagonia.

text.p: Argentine scientists in Patagonia have unearthed the bones of a 90-million-year-old dinosaur related to the fearsome velociraptor depicted in the film "Jurassic Park", a newspaper reported on Wednesday.

"We know it was a medium-sized, carnivorous animal, about eight feet (2.5 m) long from its head to the tip of its tail, and that it weighed about 66 pounds (30 kg)," paleontologist Fernando Novas told Clarin newspaper.
The araucanoraptor argentinus was a distant relative both of the fleet-footed velociraptor and of the earliest ancestors of modern birds.

"Basically what we found in the paleontological site near the town of Plaza Huincul is the skeleton of a foot, rather complete and very well preserved," Novas said. "But this fossil provides us with much interesting data."

The fossilized remains also show similarities to other finds in Mongolia and Canada, Novas said, indicating that dinosaurs from the northern and southern hemispheres may have been more closely related than long thought.
Araucanoraptor argentinus is just the latest addition to scientists' rapidly expanding knowledge of the pre-historic inhabitants of Patagonia in southern Argentina.
In May, Novas reported the discovery of the most bird-like dinosaur known, unenlagia comahuensis, an ostrich-sized meat-eater which ran around flapping wing-like forearms to keep its balance.
The same month, Argentine scientists at the U.S. Academy of Natural Sciences unveiled the reconstructed skull of the largest carnivorous dinosaur ever found.
The dagger-toothed giganotosaurus carolinii roamed around Patagonia 97 million years ago. It was about 46 feet (14 metres) long and weighed up to eight tons.
